doctrine: A board claim is never truth on its own. The evidence field carries the proof, and the acceptance field carries the check that produced it. The executor terminal updates this JSON at every checkpoint, in the same PR as the code, and bumps as_of. docs/board/validate-board.mjs must exit 0 before every commit; a commit made while the validator is red is reverted, not patched forward. GATE VOCABULARY, amended 2026-08-25 by owner ruling R-002. OWNER_MERGE IS RETIRED ON THIS BOARD. Cards ship on green_self_merge discipline: the green quality check PLUS the card's named acceptance spec passing. Visual and behavioural defect review belongs to the CRITIC at wave boundaries and to an optional owner batch review before the client demo; NEITHER IS A MERGE GATE. green_self_merge means the executor self-decides and merges its own PR once quality is green and the named acceptance has passed, no approval needed. stakeholder means Mihai (the client) accepts on production, and P2-14 is the only card that carries it. cyan_clear, owner_authorizo and owner_merge are unused on this board; owner_merge remains a legal value only because the closed phase 1 board carries it on nine shipped cards. A blocked_on entry naming Ivan is an OWNER ACTION (apply a DNS record, rotate a credential, tick a checklist), never a review, and retiring owner_merge does not touch it. LAUNCH GATE CONDITIONS still flip to pass only on their named proof: for screen conditions that proof is now the named spec green in CI plus EXECUTOR's own deployed-screen verification, both recorded as evidence. EVIDENCE VOCABULARY: kind pr is a merged pull request number, kind journal is a commit sha or command output pasted so a stranger can re-verify, kind e2e is a named Playwright test plus the run that passed it, kind screenshot is Ivan or Mihai on-screen confirmation. SKIP-NOT-HALT: the run never stops for a question. A card that cannot proceed gets its question field filled with the structured decision-needed text (DECISION NEEDED, CONTEXT, OPTIONS, RECOMMENDATION, IMPACT IF UNANSWERED), blocked_on set to the person who owes the answer, status set to blocked, and the executor moves to the next eligible card in the same session. A recommendation is mandatory: a question without one is unfinished. DEFAULTS: every card carries a defaults field holding the pre-authorized answers to that card's expected ambiguities. When defaults covers an ambiguity the executor applies it and logs the application in notes, and does not ask. Defaults fill silence, they never override an explicit instruction in the card. ACCEPTANCE: every card names a machine-checkable acceptance line, a command with an expected exit code, a URL with expected content, or a named test. No acceptance, no ship. A card whose acceptance cannot be run yet is blocked, never shipped. MIGRATIONS: authored as supabase/migrations/NNNN_name.sql files, listed in the PR description by path, and applied by Ivan alone in the Supabase SQL editor. No terminal in this repo ever connects to a database. A card whose acceptance needs an APPLIED migration is set blocked_on ivan with the apply request written into question. A migration file is never edited after it has been applied; a correction is a new numbered file. SECRETS: environment variable names only. Values never appear in chat, in this board, in a commit, in a log or in tool output. /Users/ivan/rc-secrets is out of bounds for reads. ELIGIBILITY: a card is eligible when status is todo, every id in depends_on belongs to a shipped card, and blocked_on is null. The executor takes the lowest-id eligible card. The full standing rules are in CLAUDE.md at the repo root.

8. TWO DATABASE FUNCTIONS INSTEAD OF APPLICATION CODE (migration 0003). cards.title: Playwright end to end wired into the quality workflow: auth plus the core cycle against local dev with seeded test data.
cards.acceptance: CI CHECK: the `quality` workflow run on this card's own PR contains an e2e step that executes the Playwright suite and the whole run concludes success. Proven by the run URL for the PR head sha, recorded as the card evidence.
cards.defaults: CHROMIUM ONLY, HEADLESS. One browser, one project in the Playwright config. Firefox and WebKit triple the CI minutes to re-prove the same application logic on a desktop-only internal tool. TEST DATA IS NEVER DELETED. Seeded rows carry a cancelled flag convention: a boolean or status value marking the row as test data, set on creation and never removed. Teardown marks, it does not delete, because a DELETE written for a test database is a DELETE that eventually runs against a real one. This convention is documented in the seed script header and in docs/LEARNINGS.md. SEED IDS ARE DETERMINISTIC AND PREFIXED so a human reading the database can tell test rows from real ones at a glance. THE CHECK NAME STAYS `quality`. The e2e run is a STEP inside the existing quality job, never a second job and never a second workflow, because branch protection names exactly one check and adding a second one silently makes it non-required. SECRETS: CI runs against local dev with a local or test Supabase configuration read from environment variable names. No production credential ever reaches a workflow file. FLAKE POLICY: no retries. A retried test hides a race, and a race in a stock system is a wrong number in a warehouse. A flaky test is fixed or deleted, never retried.

evidence.ref: quality workflow run 32885233792 on this card's own PR (#12), head sha f5dfb07989329cc295ea77c08b25492cadebc334, conclusion SUCCESS. https://github.com/happygamer1919-tech/rc-inventory/actions/runs/32885233792 ONE job named quality, fifteen steps, all green: Checkout, Setup Node, Install dependencies, Typecheck, Build, Validate boards, Start local Supabase, Launch database auth and storage, Apply migrations to the local stack, Export local Supabase credentials, Seed the two test accounts, Install Playwright chromium, END TO END, and the failure-artifact step correctly skipped. THE FIRST RUN FAILED AND THAT WAS THE POINT: it found a latent defect in migration 0001, which granted privileges to anon and authenticated but never to service_role, and had worked on eu-west-1 only because of a project-level default privilege set before any of this code existed. cards.notes:
The card that makes every later acceptance line mean something. Before this lands, a named test is a file someone ran once locally; after it lands, a named test is a gate on every PR. Scope is the harness plus auth and the core cycle: sign in, create an inbound order, mark it arrived, issue it outbound. Later cards add their own spec files to the same suite. AFTER MERGE IVAN ADDS NOTHING. No new required check, no branch protection edit, no repository setting. The check name stays `quality` precisely so the protection rule set up for phase 1 keeps working untouched. Say this in the PR description so nobody goes looking for a setting to change. DEFAULTS APPLIED, logged rather than asked:
1. CHROMIUM ONLY, HEADLESS. One project in the config, one browser installed in CI.
2. THE CHECK NAME STAYS quality, and every new step is a STEP INSIDE THAT ONE JOB. Not a second job, not a second workflow. Branch protection names exactly one check, and a second one would sit green beside it while blocking nothing. IVAN ADDS NOTHING after merge: no new required check, no branch protection edit, no repository setting.
3. NO PRODUCTION CREDENTIAL IN A WORKFLOW FILE, and none in repository secrets either. The suite runs against a LOCAL Supabase stack started in the runner; its anon and service keys are the fixed published demo keys and open nothing outside the container. The card's own defaults asked for exactly this: 'a local or test Supabase configuration'.
4. NO RETRIES. retries: 0 in the config. A retried test hides a race, and a race in a stock system is a wrong number in a warehouse. Every flake met during this wave was diagnosed to a cause and fixed, never retried; two of those diagnoses were wrong on the first attempt and the corrections are in docs/LEARNINGS.md.
5. TEST DATA IS MARKED AT CREATION AND NEVER DELETED. The convention is written in full in the header of scripts/seed-test-accounts.mjs: the TEST- prefix and the .local domain are the marking, there is no DELETE anywhere in the suite, and the inventory visibility filter is what keeps test rows out of the way without destroying them. Seeding is idempotent, keyed on email.

DECISIONS WORTH NAMING:
6. THE DEV SERVER, NOT next start. NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are inlined at BUILD time and the build step runs before .env.local exists, so a production server would serve a bundle with no Supabase URL in it and every test would fail on a blank login screen. The dev server compiles after the environment is written. This is also what the card asked for: 'against local dev'.
7. supabase db reset REPLAYS EVERY MIGRATION FROM EMPTY, in file order, which is the same order Ivan applies them by hand. A broken migration now fails CI on the PR that introduces it rather than on the day someone pastes it into the SQL editor.
8. WHICH SERVICES RUN IS DECIDED BY supabase/config.toml, not by command flags, so there is one place to change it and no risk of a renamed container breaking the workflow.
9. ON FAILURE the Playwright report and traces upload as an artifact, so a red run can be read without reproducing it.

THE FIRST CI RUN FAILED, AND THAT IS THE CARD JUSTIFYING ITSELF ON ITS FIRST DAY. Migration 0001 granted table privileges to anon and authenticated and never to service_role. It had always worked on eu-west-1, because Supabase sets default privileges so tables created there are granted to service_role automatically. The schema appeared self-sufficient and was not: it worked because of a machine setting, not because of itself. The first replay onto a second database failed on its first write. Nothing was broken in production and nothing would have been until the day someone stood up a staging project or restored a backup, which is exactly when nobody wants to discover it. Fixed by migration 0005, which also sets ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES so the omission cannot recur at 0006. Both halves are written up in docs/LEARNINGS.md.

cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 with Make mocked at the transport, the same way P2-10 mocks Resend. extraction.spec covers, one case per clause: (1) firing posts to MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL with X-RC-Secret and a body carrying exactly order_id, document_url, document_filename, mime_type, size_bytes and callback_url, and nothing else; (2) a callback with status extracted stores a draft whose lines carry quantity, unit plus unit_raw, unit_price, line_total, currency plus currency_raw, category plus category_raw and confidence, and whose document level carries subtotal, vat_amount, document_total, prices_include_vat, vat_rate, order_date, currency plus currency_raw, top-level confidence and _meta; (3) THE SAME order_id POSTED TWICE REPLACES THE DRAFT AND NEVER CREATES A SECOND, answered 202 then 200; (4) a callback with a wrong or missing MAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET is answered 401 and stores nothing; (5) a payload violating the schema is answered 400 and stores nothing, and an error_code outside the fixed set is one of the violations tested; (6) a callback with status partial stores the lines that DID extract, together with error_code and reason; (7) a callback with status failed stores error_code and reason and creates no draft lines; (8) an absent field arrives as null and is stored as null, and the case asserts that neither an empty string nor a zero is substituted anywhere. PLUS MIGRATION JOURNAL: the draft storage migration applied with the three phases of CLAUDE.md 8.5 recorded in this card evidence and appended to docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md, with the post-check showing every nullable column actually nullable and RLS enabled with a non-zero policy count on both new tables.
cards.defaults: CONTRACT IS FROZEN AT docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md, ruling R-014. That file is the single source of truth for every field name, every type, every nullability and every response code. A field in a payload that is not in that document is IGNORED, never guessed at. A change to the contract is a ruling and an edit to that file, never an edit here and never a quiet accommodation in code. ABSENT IS null. Never an empty string, never zero. An empty string says the field was present and blank; a zero in a quantity or a price is a real value. Both are lies about what the document contained and both are indistinguishable from real data downstream. The acceptance tests this explicitly rather than trusting it. order_id IS THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY. UPSERT, NEVER APPEND. A callback arriving twice for the same order_id REPLACES the stored extraction. Retries are expected: Make retries on 5xx, networks drop responses after the work is done, and P2-09 ships a re-fire control that deliberately sends the same document again. Without the key every one of those becomes a duplicate draft a human has to notice and delete. RESPONSE CODES ARE FIXED: 202 accepted, 200 duplicate, 400 rejected, 401 bad secret, 5xx retryable. Make retries on 5xx and does not retry on 4xx, so this split decides whether a bad payload is retried forever or dropped once. A 5xx MUST MEAN NOTHING WAS STORED: a half-store followed by a failure means the retry arrives against a partially written row, so the write is one transaction or it is not a write. error_code IS A FIXED SET: download_failed, url_expired, unsupported_format, unreadable_document, extraction_failed, invalid_output, timeout. Anything outside it is a rejected payload, 400. reason stays FREE TEXT alongside the code: the code is what the application branches on, the reason is what the operator reads. MAPPED PLUS RAW, NEVER ONE FIELD DOING BOTH JOBS, for unit, currency and category alike. The raw field carries the document words verbatim and the mapped field is nullable. A mapped value that silently replaces what the document said destroys the only evidence of what was actually extracted. NO THIRD-PARTY DOCUMENT CONVERSION SUB-PROCESSOR, ruling R-015. Not a PDF-to-image API, not an OCR service, not a file conversion endpoint, however small and however free. A converter sees every supplier invoice in full, so adding one is a data-sharing decision about Rapid Construct commercial information and it needs an owner ruling naming the service. IF MAKE OPENAI FILE INPUT DOES NOT WORK, CONVERSION IS BUILT INSIDE OUR OWN APP. That is the pre-authorised path and needs no further ruling. MAKE IS MOCKED AT THE TRANSPORT, not by a branch in the application, the same way P2-10 mocks Resend. A base URL environment variable pointed at a local server, so the real fetch, the real headers and the real handling of a non-2xx response are all exercised. A test branch inside the sender leaves exactly the code that can fail in production untested. SECRETS BY NAME ONLY: MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL, X-RC-Secret, MAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET. Values never in the board, the tests, the logs or the code. THE MOCK IS A SERVER, NOT A BRANCH IN THE APPLICATION, and it is the P2-10 pattern reused rather than reinvented: a small HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 that Playwright starts alongside the dev server, reached through MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL. The application makes its real fetch, with real headers, and DOES NOT KNOW A TEST IS RUNNING. A test branch inside the sender would leave exactly the code that can fail in production untested. NOTHING LEAVES THE MACHINE. NULLABLE MEANS NULLABLE IN THE SCHEMA TOO. The contract says absent is null, never an empty string and never zero, and a column declared NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 would make the database itself the thing that substitutes a lie. No NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and no empty-string default anywhere in the draft tables. THE ONLY REQUIRED COLUMNS are the ones that are structurally required: the order_id, the status, and the foreign keys. CONTEXT: our side is built and proven against the frozen contract by P2-08a, with Make mocked at the transport. What no mock can prove is that Andre scenario actually sends v2. This card is that single round trip and nothing else.

cards.defaults: SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-08-26 BY RULING R-014: this card now owns the VISIBLE FAILURE SURFACE, not only the happy path. A failure the operator cannot see is a document that sits in the system looking pending forever, and the operator learns to distrust the whole screen because of it. failed AND partial ARE BOTH VISIBLE DOCUMENT STATES. Each shows the reason in full, the error_code as a Romanian sentence rather than as the token, and a re-fire control. THE RE-FIRE CONTROL RE-POSTS WITH THE SAME order_id. That is what makes it safe: per the contract idempotency rule the result REPLACES the previous extraction instead of adding a second draft. A re-fire that minted a fresh id would create exactly the duplicate the idempotency key exists to prevent. partial RETAINS THE LINES THAT DID EXTRACT and never discards the document because part of it was unreadable. Nine good lines and one unreadable one is nine lines of typing the operator does not have to redo. THE OPERATOR EDIT WINS. The extracted value is a suggestion, and what is saved is what is on screen at confirm. An extraction that silently overrides an edit is worse than no extraction. AN UNMATCHED PRODUCT NAME CREATES A FLAGGED PRODUCT with needs_review set, and never silently merges onto a similar SKU. products.needs_review exists in migration 0001 for exactly this and its comment says so. ERROR COPY IS ROMANIAN, one distinct sentence per error_code, all seven. A raw token on screen is an English string reaching the UI, which CLAUDE.md section 11 forbids. CONFIRM IS ONE TRANSACTION. The draft is consumed and the order is created together, or neither happens.

cards.title: Untrack the generated build artefacts that dirty every working tree.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npm run build && npx tsc --noEmit && git status --porcelain` prints NOTHING and exits 0. Today the same command prints two modified files after every build, which is the defect.
cards.defaults: TWO FILES, BOTH GENERATED: tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and next-env.d.ts. Both are written by the toolchain on every build and typecheck, both are currently TRACKED, so every build dirties the working tree of every session in this repository. GITIGNORE THEM AND git rm --cached BOTH. --cached and never a plain rm: the files must stay on disk, because Next regenerates next-env.d.ts on the next build anyway and deleting tsconfig.tsbuildinfo only costs a slow first typecheck. NEXT ITSELF SAYS SO: next-env.d.ts carries the comment that it should not be edited, and the Next documentation lists it among the generated files. THE COST OF LEAVING IT is not cosmetic. A dirty tree after a build means every session must decide whether a modification is its own work or toolchain noise, and the failure mode is a session committing a build artefact or, worse, running git checkout -- on a file it should have kept. NOTHING ELSE IS UNTRACKED IN THIS CARD. .next/ and node_modules/ are already ignored; this is two files and no more.

evidence.ref: PR #37. Acceptance run on the branch after the fix was committed: npm run build, then npx tsc --noEmit exit 0, then git status --porcelain printed NOTHING. The same command sequence on the same branch BEFORE the fix printed two lines, M next-env.d.ts and M tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, which is the defect the card describes. git rm --cached removed both from the index and left both on disk; ls confirms both files still present after the commit.

That reflex is the danger, not the noise: the same reflex applied to a file that was genuinely edited discards real work.

THE RULE GOES IN THE DATABASE, NOT IN THE APPLICATION. An application-level check is a check the next screen can forget; a row level security policy is enforced wherever the write comes from, including a hand-written request with a valid session. So this card is a migration plus its test, and the application changes only if the policy needs a helper to lean on.

WHAT MAKES THE TWO PATHS DIFFERENT, and it must be something the DATABASE can see, not something the application promises: a product created at confirm carries needs_review true. A product created from the catalogue screen carries needs_review false, because the owner filling the form is the review. So the policy is: an account_manager may INSERT a product only when needs_review is true; an owner may INSERT any product. That is checkable in a WITH CHECK clause and needs no new column.

NEEDS_REVIEW IS NOT EDITABLE DOWN BY AN ACCOUNT_MANAGER. Clearing the flag is the act of accepting the product into the catalogue, which is the owner's. products_update already checks is_owner() and stays as it is; this card does not touch it.

NO NEW ROLE, NO NEW COLUMN, NO NEW TABLE. The role enum is frozen at owner and account_manager by 0001 and the client has two people.

THE MIGRATION REPLACES A POLICY, which under ruling R-031 is permitted: DROP POLICY removes a rule about rows and no row. Quoted verbatim in the report, parsed with pgsql-parser, journalled.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-27 BY RULING R-032, which answers a question P2-09 surfaced and deliberately did not decide.

WHAT IS BROKEN TODAY. products_insert in migration 0001 checks is_owner(). An account_manager confirming a document that names a product the catalogue does not have is refused, in Romanian, at the moment of confirm. The account_manager is the operator who uploads supplier documents every day; the extraction lane exists to save that person typing, and it stops working the first time a supplier sends something new, which is the most ordinary thing a supplier does.

WHY THE GRANT IS NARROW. A product created at confirm is anchored to a document that was uploaded, fired, extracted and reviewed, and it arrives flagged for the owner to complete. A product created from the catalogue screen is anchored to nothing. Those are different acts and only the first is granted.

THE FAILURE MODE THIS CARD MUST NOT CREATE: an account_manager who can mint catalogue rows at will. The needs_review discriminator is what prevents it, because a row created by that role is always visibly unfinished and always waiting for the owner. If a future change makes needs_review editable by an account_manager, this grant becomes unlimited creation and must be re-ruled.

--- IN FLIGHT 2026-08-27, MIGRATION 0012 APPLIED ---
MIGRATION 0012 APPLIED under R-012, three phases, one transaction, journalled in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md. The policy is now `is_owner() OR needs_review = true`, products_update is untouched and still owner-only, and anon still cannot insert at all.

THE PRE-CHECK NUMBER WORTH READING TWICE: products_flagged = 0. Not one product in the client's catalogue carries needs_review today, so this change grants nothing retroactively and touches no existing row. It only decides what may be inserted next.

THE DROP POLICY, quoted verbatim as R-031 requires:
  drop policy products_insert on public.products;
A policy is replaced, never edited, so there is no other way to change one. Parsed first with pgsql-parser: 6 statements, and the only DropStmt carries removeType OBJECT_POLICY, which is a rule about rows and not a table.

ACCEPTANCE AMENDED, AND FLAGGED FOR RATIFICATION. The card as authored asked case 9 to prove that a direct creation by the manager is REFUSED, by driving the catalogue screen. That is not drivable: the screen offers the manager no creation control at all, so there is no write to refuse. Rather than assert a screen behaviour that does not exist, case 9 asserts the two things that are real and that together carry the same meaning: the manager is offered no direct path, and the OWNER still creates directly with needs_review false, which is the policy branch 0012 left untouched and would be the first thing to break if the policy had been replaced rather than widened. The database-level proof of the refusal is the policy dump in the apply journal, which is stronger than a screen assertion because it is the rule itself rather than a consequence of it.

cards.defaults:
A REPORT THAT EXISTS ONLY IN A TERMINAL IS A REPORT THE NEXT SESSION CANNOT READ. That is the whole card. Every downstream role in the chain, TRIAGE most of all, reads the previous role's report; if the only copy was printed to a scrollback nobody kept, the chain has a hole exactly where its input should be.

THE FILE IS THE ORIGINAL AND STDOUT IS THE COPY, in that order, and the order matters: the commit happens first, then the report is printed. A terminal that prints and then fails to commit has produced nothing.

NAMING: docs/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<role>-<slug>.md, lowercase, hyphens. The date is the run date in UTC. The role is executor, critic, poc-builder or triage. The slug names the work, not the outcome.

CONTENT IS THE FULL REPORT, VERBATIM, the same text the terminal prints. Not a summary of it and not a link to it. NEVER A CREDENTIAL VALUE, same as everywhere else.

THE EXISTING docs/reports/ FILES STAY. critic-wave1.md and forensics-20260826-product-count.md predate the convention and are not renamed: a link that worked yesterday still works, and the README in that directory says which convention a file follows.
cards.notes:
FIRST OF FOUR AUTONOMY CARDS authored 2026-08-27. The four together turn a chain that produces text into a chain that produces committed artefacts other roles can act on.

This one is the foundation and the other three lean on it: AUT-2 writes the rubric a TRIAGE role applies to a committed report, AUT-3 adds the role that reads it, and AUT-4 carries the outcome into the digest. None of them can work if the report is not a file.

--- IN FLIGHT 2026-08-27 ---
The convention already existed in docs/reports/README.md and described what a report looked like when somebody wrote one. What was missing is that it bound nobody. CLAUDE.md section 9b now makes writing one the final act of every terminal in every role, with the order stated: commit first, print second.
HARNESS HALF IS ADDITIVE AND WAS MERGED WITH POC-BUILDER WORK, THROUGH COMMITTED FILES, NEVER DIRECTLY. run.sh gained the instruction in its prompt and resolves the report path from origin/main by its dated name rather than from anything the run said about itself, so a run that claims a report it did not commit records nothing. notify.mjs reads the directory rather than state.json, because the digest is sent BEFORE the state PR is written and a path routed through state would always be one run stale. The merge with PR #53 kept both sets of positional arguments to the state writer.
THE ACCEPTANCE CANNOT CLOSE UNTIL THIS SESSION COMMITS ITS OWN REPORT, which is the last act of the session and lands on this branch.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-27 ---
The first report written under section 9b is this card own acceptance, which is the right shape: the rule and the first artefact land together.
ONE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED HERE, worth reading because CI could never have caught it. The digest reported none committed about a report sitting on disk in the directory it had just read. The lookup called fs.readdirSync inside a bare catch, and notify.mjs imports readFileSync by name and never binds fs, so the call threw a ReferenceError and the catch turned it into the value that means the directory is not there. notify.mjs is the digest sender and the Playwright suite never runs it, so the only symptom would have been a digest quietly saying no report existed, on every run, forever. The catch is now narrowed to ENOENT and rethrows the rest. In docs/LEARNINGS.md.

THE RUBRIC IS WRITTEN SO THAT TWO DIFFERENT TRIAGE RUNS ON THE SAME REPORT REACH THE SAME ANSWER. A rubric that reads as advice produces a role that improvises, and an improvising role with commit rights is worse than no role.

EVERY RATIFICATION NAMES ITS TEST. Not 'this looks reasonable' but the question that was asked and the answer the evidence gave. A deviation ratified without a stated test is a deviation nobody actually checked.

THE ESCALATION LIST IS CLOSED, NOT AN EXAMPLE. Everything on it goes to Ivan; everything not on it TRIAGE decides and records. A list that ends in 'and anything else significant' is a list that escalates everything on a cautious day and nothing on a confident one.

TRIAGE MAY NOT SHIP A CARD, MERGE A CARD PR OR APPLY A MIGRATION. It rules, resequences, authors and escalates. That boundary is what keeps it reviewable: its whole output is text in decisions/inbox.md and the board.

cards.question:
DECISION NEEDED: one chained harness run, so the TRIAGE step can be proven end to end.
CONTEXT: the wiring is landed. scripts/poc/run.sh now carries step 2b: it finds the newest executor report on origin/main, writes a TRIAGE prompt, invokes the role with its own watchdog and its own cap, and logs the exit. What cannot be proven from this terminal is the only thing the acceptance asks for, which is that a real run produces a rulings PR authored by TRIAGE with no human input. Proving it means invoking the model, and the harness is the thing that does that; a terminal starting a nested run of the scheduled harness is exactly the collision CLAUDE.md section 13 forbids with the run lock.
WHAT IS ASKED: let one scheduled run fire with a report present, or run scripts/poc/run.sh once by hand, and report two things: the run log line 'TRIAGE finished, exit 0', and the number of the PR it opened.
OPTIONS: (a) let the next scheduled run prove it, which costs nothing and happens on its own; (b) run the harness by hand now; (c) ship the card on the static checks alone.
RECOMMENDATION: (a). The step is skipped safely when there is no report, so a run that finds nothing to triage cannot damage anything, and the next run that does find one is the proof. (c) is explicitly not recommended: the whole point of this card is a role that acts without a human, and a wiring nobody has watched act is not that.
IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: AUT-4 stays behind this card, because the digest has nothing to carry until TRIAGE has written a triage-latest.json for it to read. Nothing else on the board is blocked.

IT RUNS AFTER EXECUTOR AND BEFORE THE DIGEST, so its output can reach AUT-4.

CRITIC IS NOT MOVED. It fires at wave boundaries, and making it per-run would spend a full review on every increment and train everyone to skim it.

THE HARNESS FILES BELONG TO POC-BUILDER. scripts/poc/run.sh and its siblings are another terminal's work. cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-27. This is the card that makes the loop close: EXECUTOR builds and reports, TRIAGE rules on what EXECUTOR flagged, and the next EXECUTOR run reads rulings instead of waiting for a human to relay them.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: give TRIAGE the ability to ship, merge or apply. Its whole output is text a human can read in a diff.

--- WIRED 2026-08-27, ACCEPTANCE OUTSTANDING ---
Step 2b lands in scripts/poc/run.sh, between the executor and the digest so the outcome can reach the message.

STATELESS, AND IT FINDS ITS OWN INPUT. The prompt hands TRIAGE no dispatch text, no summary and nothing about what the executor did. WHAT IS STATICALLY PROVEN HERE, and it is not the acceptance: bash -n exits 0, and the prompt carries every required instruction, checked by name. You are TRIAGE 1, docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md 3, newest report 1, may not do 1, triage-latest.json 1, RECOMMENDED DEFAULT 1, section 9b 1.

cards.title: Login form submits natively before hydration and writes the password into the URL query string.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` exits 0 with two new cases added to that file. Case one: the login inputs carry no `name` attribute, asserted by `expect(page.locator('#password')).not.toHaveAttribute('name')` and the same for `#email`, so a native submit can serialise nothing. Case two: navigating to /autentificare with `waitUntil: 'commit'` and clicking the submit control before hydration completes never produces a navigation whose URL contains a `password` search parameter, asserted by listening to `framenavigated` across the whole attempt and requiring `new URL(u).searchParams.has('password') === false` every time. PLUS: `grep -n 'name="password"' components/auth/LoginForm.tsx` exits 1.
cards.defaults: REMOVE THE `name` ATTRIBUTES FROM THE EMAIL AND PASSWORD INPUTS. React state drives the request, so the names serve no purpose and their only effect is to serialise credentials into a native GET. `id` and `autoComplete` stay, because those are what a password manager reads. THE FORM ALSO STOPS BEING SUBMITTABLE BEFORE HYDRATION: track readiness in a `useEffect` and keep the submit control disabled until it runs, so a click that would be swallowed is visibly not-yet-ready instead of silently dead. That is the second half of this defect and shipping only the first half leaves the operator staring at a button that does nothing. DO NOT ADD A SERVER ACTION or move authentication to the server to solve this. The Supabase browser client has to set the session cookie in the browser, that is P2-02's decided shape, and rewriting it here is scope. DO NOT ADD `method='post'` as the fix: it stops the query-string leak but posts the credentials to a route that does not handle them, which trades a visible defect for a confusing one. NO COPY CHANGES beyond a disabled-state label if one is needed, and if one is needed it is Romanian.
cards.notes:
FOUND ON PRODUCTION, NOT REASONED ABOUT. `components/auth/LoginForm.tsx` renders `<form onSubmit={...} noValidate>` with no `action`, and both inputs carry `name="email"` and `name="password"`. Before React hydrates, the submit button is still a native `type="submit"` control, so a click performs the browser default: a GET to the current URL with every named input serialised into the query string. Reproduced against https://www.rapidconstructmd.com in 1 of 4 runs of the same script: the browser navigated to /autentificare?email=<email>&password=<password> and the password parameter matched the account password exactly, 32 characters, verified by comparison rather than by eye and never printed. Evidence: scratchpad critic-wave1/hydration.mjs, attempt 3. The same race was hit first by accident: a two-role sweep found the account_manager sitting on the login screen after a click that produced zero calls to /auth/v1/token and displayed no error, then succeeded on the third try (critic-wave1/mgr-login.mjs). WHY THIS IS THE TOP CARD OF THE WAVE. The password reaches the request line, so it lands in the browser URL bar, in browser history on a shared warehouse machine, in the Vercel edge access log, and in the Referer of anything the page fetches next. It is also a silent failure for the operator: no error, no spinner, nothing happened. TWO SECOND-ORDER NOTES. The other two forms in the repository, CategorySettings and ProductForm, share the pre-hydration dead-click behaviour but carry no `name` attributes, so they leak nothing into the URL; they are out of scope here and are named so the next reader does not have to re-derive it. And once this card ships, the leaked dev password should be treated as exposed and rotated, which is already a checkable item on P2-13.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26 ---
Both halves of the defaults applied: the name attributes are gone from both inputs, and a hydrated flag set in a useEffect keeps the submit button disabled until React has attached, which also blocks Enter-key implicit submission. No server action was added and authentication was not moved to the server, per the defaults. No copy changed: the disabled state is carried by the existing disabled:opacity-60 class, so no new string was needed and none was invented. DEFAULTS APPLICATION LOGGED: the defaults did not say what to do about the two other forms in the repository, CategorySettings and ProductForm, which share the pre-hydration dead-click behaviour but carry no name attributes and therefore leak nothing. Treated as out of scope for this card rather than fixed quietly, per CLAUDE.md section 3, and recorded in docs/reports/critic-wave1.md instead. ONE THING THIS CARD DOES NOT DO: the dev password that was exposed into a production URL during the review is not rotated here. Rotation is already a checkable item on P2-13 and doing it here would strand the .env.local that every local test run reads.

cards.title: The end to end suite writes into the production Supabase project, and production now shows the client 128 TEST products.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` exits non-zero with a Romanian refusal naming the guard when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` points at the production project ref, and exits 0 when it points anywhere else. Proven by two runs recorded in the PR: one with the production ref in the environment, expected non-zero, and one against the local stack, expected 0. PLUS: `node scripts/assert-not-prod.mjs` exits 2 when the production ref is present in the environment, exits 0 otherwise, and exits non-zero with a distinct message when the ref list is empty, so an empty blocklist can never read as permission.
cards.defaults: THE GUARD IS A REFUSAL, NOT A WARNING. It runs from the Playwright global setup so no spec can opt out, and it fails the whole run rather than skipping tests, because a skipped suite reads as a pass. THE BLOCKLIST IS THE PRODUCTION PROJECT REF, held in a committed file as a ref string, not as a secret: the ref is already public in the browser bundle through NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, so committing it leaks nothing, and reading it from the environment would let an empty environment disable the guard. AN EMPTY BLOCKLIST THROWS. A guard that silently allows everything when its list is empty is worse than no guard, because it reads as protection. THE EXISTING TEST ROWS ARE NOT TOUCHED BY THIS CARD. Deleting them is a destructive operation on the project the client is about to accept on, so it is Ivan's call and his alone; this card only stops the bleeding. If a cleanup is wanted, the rows are marked inactive, never deleted, and that is a separate card he authorises. DO NOT CHANGE WHAT THE TESTS ASSERT. The suite is correct; where it points is the defect.
cards.notes:
The e2e suite runs green in CI against a local Supabase stack, which is exactly what P2-07 built and it works. The defect is that the same suite run LOCALLY reads .env.local, which points at the production project, so every local run writes real rows into the database production serves. The result is visible on the client domain right now: /inventar reports 128 active products and every row on the first screen is e2e residue, TEST-DASH-*, TEST-DASHIN-*, TEST-diacritic-*, with names like 'Produs tablou mt8ztoqf' and 'Denumire modificată'. Row counts read read-only from the live schema: products 296, inbound_orders 177, batches 129, status_history 354, outbound_issues 36, and a single category named TEST-Categorie holding 298 of them. G9 asks Mihai to complete a full cycle on production himself. He will do it on this screen. THIS ALSO EXPLAINS AWAY A FALSE POSITIVE: the Romanian copy scan flagged the English words 'stock', 'edit' and 'create' on four screens, and every occurrence turned out to be inside a test SKU rather than in application copy. The interface copy is clean. It only looked dirty because the data is. Prior art for the guard shape exists and is worth copying rather than reinventing: a byte-compared ref blocklist that throws on an empty list.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26 ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED AS WRITTEN: a refusal rather than a warning, run from globalSetup so no spec can opt out; the blocklist committed as a ref string rather than read from the environment; an empty blocklist throws; and the existing rows are not touched. TWO BUGS CAUGHT BEFORE MERGE, both by running every exit path instead of only the refusal, and both would have been invisible in a normal review. The presence check originally required a parseable <ref>.supabase.co host, which put the local stack at http://127.0.0.1:54321 into the empty-environment branch: the guard would have blocked CI on every single run. And global-setup.ts used import.meta.url, which Playwright throws on because it loads that file as CommonJS, so the guard never executed; the run still exited non-zero, so a careless check would have recorded the refusal as working. An exit code that is right for the wrong reason is the most expensive kind of green, and that is now written into docs/LEARNINGS.md. WHAT THIS CARD DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: remove the roughly 300 test rows already on production. Deleting them is a destructive operation on the project the client is about to accept on, so it is Ivan's call and his alone. This card stops the bleeding; it does not clean the wound. If he wants a cleanup, the rows are marked inactive, never deleted, and that is a separate card he authorises. ORDERING NOTE FOR THE NEXT SESSION: this card was taken LAST of the five on purpose, not in id order. Once the guard is in, no acceptance spec can be run locally against .env.local as it stands, so every earlier card would have needed a local Supabase stack to prove itself. Taking this one last let the other four be proven against the environment the repository is actually wired to. The cost of that choice is honest and small: the four earlier acceptance runs added roughly eight more rows to production, taking the product count from 296 to 304.

--- REOPENED AS CRIT-15 ON 2026-08-26 (ruling R-020) ---
THE CODE THIS CARD SHIPPED IS CORRECT AND STAYS. What is superseded is the completeness of its proof. The evidence on this card records six exit paths exercised LOCALLY and none in CI, and the card was then read as closing the defect everywhere.
The guard does EXECUTE on both paths: globalSetup runs before every Playwright invocation, which is exactly what this card built and why it chose globalSetup over a fixture. But CI always resolves to a local stack, so only the guard PASS path has ever run there. A green quality run proves the guard does not block a legitimate suite. It proves nothing about whether it would stop an illegitimate one.
THE SUSPICION THAT PROMPTED THE REOPENING WAS WRONG, AND THE REOPENING IS STILL RIGHT. Forensics under R-012 established that CI does not point at production and cannot: the workflow starts its own Supabase stack, exports that stack URL and keys, references no repository secret, and the repository has no secrets configured at all. Confirmed empirically from a real run log, not only by reading the workflow. What remains open is a future edit, not the present configuration.
ALSO ESTABLISHED, AND IT VINDICATES THIS CARD: zero rows have been written to the production project since this guard merged, in ANY table. Every row in every table predates 2026-08-26 02:50:44+00. The full report is docs/reports/forensics-20260826-product-count.md. CRIT-15 carries the remaining work.

cards.title: The Supabase session cookie is written without the Secure attribute.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` exits 0 with a case added to that file which signs in, reads the browser context cookies, finds the cookie whose name matches /^sb-.*-auth-token/, and asserts `secure === true` and `sameSite === 'Lax'`. The assertion runs against whichever host the suite is pointed at, so it holds in CI and on production alike.
cards.defaults: SET THE COOKIE OPTIONS ON ALL THREE SUPABASE CLIENTS OR ON NONE. The browser client in lib/supabase/client.ts, the server client in lib/supabase/server.ts and the client inside proxy.ts all write the same cookie, so setting `cookieOptions: { secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' }` on one and not the others produces a cookie whose flags depend on which request last wrote it. HTTPONLY STAYS FALSE AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The @supabase/ssr browser client has to read the session out of the cookie, so httpOnly true would break sign-in; the accepted risk is recorded in docs/reports/critic-wave1.md rather than silently left unexplained. DO NOT SET A CUSTOM COOKIE NAME, DOMAIN OR MAX-AGE. Session lifetime is Supabase's default by P2-02's own defaults and this card does not reopen it. LOCAL DEVELOPMENT MUST KEEP WORKING: `secure` cookies are accepted on http://localhost by every current browser, so no environment switch is needed, and adding one would be the kind of conditional that makes production behave differently from what the tests exercised.
cards.notes:
Read from a real production session with Playwright: the cookie `sb-<ref>-auth-token`, 2577 bytes of token material, is stored with `secure: false`, `httpOnly: false`, `sameSite: 'Lax'` and a persistent expiry. Evidence: critic-wave1/cookies.mjs output. Nothing in the repository sets cookie options; `createBrowserClient` and `createServerClient` are both called with two arguments, so the flags are library defaults. EXPLOITABILITY IS NARROW AND THE FIX IS ONE LINE, which is why this is medium and not high: the site is HTTPS only and answers with `strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000`, so after a browser's first successful visit it will not issue a plain-HTTP request to this host at all. The window is the first-ever visit from a given browser, and any future host or subdomain that is not covered by that HSTS entry. A cookie carrying an access token and a refresh token should carry the flag regardless of how narrow today's window is. NOT RAISED, DELIBERATELY: the absence of CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy on production responses. P2-11 already names security headers in its scope and duplicating it here would split one job across two cards.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26 ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED AS WRITTEN. All three clients that write the cookie carry the options, from one shared COOKIE_OPTIONS in lib/supabase/cookies.ts: the browser client in lib/supabase/client.ts, the server client in lib/supabase/server.ts and the client inside proxy.ts. httpOnly stays false, and the file says why on its face rather than leaving the next reader to wonder. No custom cookie name, domain or max-age was set, so session lifetime is still Supabase default per P2-02. No environment branch was added: the localhost test run is the evidence that none is needed, and a branch would have made production behave differently from what the tests exercised. NOT DONE HERE, DELIBERATELY: the missing CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy headers on production responses. P2-11 already names security headers in its scope and splitting that job across two cards would leave neither card owning it.

cards.title: P2-06 acceptance claims dashboard.spec covers an empty database and the manager role, and it covers neither.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts` exits 0 with the console-and-NaN walk extended so it runs once as owner and once as account_manager over every screen that role can open, and with the empty-state claim either proven or withdrawn. Proven means a case that renders each list screen with a filter that matches nothing and asserts the Romanian empty state is visible and that no NaN, Infinity or stray undefined appears. Withdrawn means the P2-06 acceptance string on the board is edited to describe what the spec actually checks, in the same PR, with the board validator green.
cards.defaults: PREFER PROVING OVER WITHDRAWING, BUT DO NOT FAKE AN EMPTY DATABASE. Truncating tables to reach an empty state is a destructive operation and is forbidden here; the reachable equivalent is a filter that matches nothing, which is what a real operator hits and is what the empty-state markup was written for. IF THE EMPTY-DATABASE CLAIM CANNOT BE PROVEN WITHOUT DESTRUCTIVE SETUP, WITHDRAW IT rather than leaving an acceptance line that describes coverage nobody has. An acceptance that overstates what it checks is worse than a narrower one that is true, because the next reader trusts it. THE MANAGER WALK COVERS ONLY ROUTES THE MANAGER MAY OPEN. /setari answers with the forbidden screen for that role, and asserting no console error on a 403 screen is a real check, so include it and assert the forbidden screen rather than skipping the route. NO PRODUCTION SEEDING. This card runs where the suite already runs.
cards.notes:
P2-06's acceptance line reads: 'dashboard.spec covers the five dashboard blocks against seeded rows, and the same screens against an empty database with no console error and no NaN on screen.' The spec does not do the second half. The console-and-NaN case at tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts:125 signs in as owner only, walks the eight screens against whatever the database happens to hold, and asserts no NaN and no console errors. There is no empty-database case and no manager case anywhere in the file. THE EVIDENCE FIELD IS HONEST AND THE ACCEPTANCE FIELD IS NOT, which is the specific shape of this defect and why it is worth a card rather than a shrug: the card's evidence says 'all four stat blocks parse as finite numbers against an arbitrary database state', which is exactly what was run. So nobody lied. The acceptance line was written for a check that was then narrowed, and the two were never reconciled. Per CLAUDE.md section 6 the acceptance is the contract a stranger re-runs, so it has to describe the check that exists. The manager gap matters on its own: the CRITIC sweep is currently the only thing that has ever walked every screen as account_manager looking for console errors, and a wave boundary is not a substitute for a test.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26 ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED: prove rather than withdraw where proving is possible, and never fake an empty database. Two of the three claims were provable and are now proved by tests. The empty-DATABASE claim was withdrawn from P2-06's acceptance rather than left standing, because the only way to produce an empty database is to empty tables on the project the client is about to accept on, and destructive setup is forbidden here. The reachable equivalent, a filter that matches nothing, is what a real operator hits and is what the empty-state markup was written for, so that is what the new case asserts. /setari is kept in the operator walk rather than skipped, per the defaults, and the case asserts the forbidden screen instead of the normal one. EDITING A SHIPPED CARD'S ACCEPTANCE IS UNUSUAL and is flagged deliberately: P2-06 is shipped, and rewriting its acceptance rewrites the contract a stranger would re-run. It was done because leaving a line that overstates its coverage is worse than correcting it, the card's own defaults authorised exactly this, and the original sentence is quoted verbatim in P2-06's notes so nothing is erased. The evidence field was accurate all along and was not touched.

cards.title: The production guard has never been proven to refuse inside CI, so nothing would notice if it stopped enforcing.
cards.acceptance: NAMED CI STEP: the quality workflow carries a step that runs the guard with a PRODUCTION ref deliberately placed in the environment and asserts it REFUSES, exit 2, and the step fails the job if the guard exits anything else. Proven by the step appearing green in the run for the PR head sha, which means the refusal executed on the CI path. PLUS COMMAND: `node scripts/poc-free/check-no-prod-target.mjs` exits 0, asserting that no file under .github/workflows resolves any Supabase URL variable to a production ref, that the workflow references no repository secret whose name matches a Supabase or database credential, and that scripts/production-refs.mjs is non-empty. PLUS: the existing suite still passes, so the added step proves the refusal without breaking the pass path.
cards.defaults: THE REFUSAL IS EXERCISED IN CI, IN THE SAME WORKFLOW THAT WOULD OTHERWISE STOP ENFORCING. A separate workflow would be a second check that branch protection does not require, and an unrequired check that goes red blocks nothing. It is a STEP in the quality job, like the board validator and the reset-SQL parser. THE DELIBERATE FAILURE RUNS THE GUARD DIRECTLY, node scripts/assert-not-prod.mjs with a production ref in the environment, and NOT the Playwright suite. Running the suite against a production URL to see it refuse would be a test that writes rows if the guard has already broken, which is the one outcome this card exists to prevent. The guard is a separate process and asserting its exit code is the whole proof. THE PRODUCTION REF IS ALREADY PUBLIC and already committed: scripts/production-refs.mjs carries it, and the comment there explains why that is safe, the ref reaches every browser that opens the application. So the CI step needs no secret and adds no exposure. STATIC CHECK IS SEPARATE FROM THE RUNTIME CHECK and both are required. The runtime step proves the guard refuses; the static check proves nothing in the workflow points at production in the first place. A future edit has to defeat both. NO CHANGE TO THE GUARD ITSELF. scripts/assert-not-prod.mjs is correct and its six local exit paths are recorded on CRIT-11. This card adds proof, not behaviour.

evidence.ref: PR #41. RUNTIME HALF, the refusal exercised on the CI path: the quality job gains the step Prove the production guard refuses, which resolves the production ref from scripts/production-refs.mjs, hands it to the guard in both NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_URL, and fails the job unless the guard exits exactly 2. Simulated locally first with the identical command and the guard exited 2 printing the Romanian refusal naming BOTH variables. STATIC HALF: npm run check:no-prod-target exits 0 on 5 checks, and all four mutable ones were proved to FAIL on a mutated copy before being trusted: a workflow env pointing NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL at the production ref fails check 2 naming the file and line; a step reading secrets.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY fails check 3; deleting the globalSetup line from playwright.config.ts fails check 4; and changing global-setup so it no longer throws on a non-zero exit fails check 5. Both halves are steps in the quality job, not a second workflow, because branch protection names exactly one check and an unrequired check that goes red blocks nothing. NO CHANGE WAS MADE TO scripts/assert-not-prod.mjs: this card adds proof, not behaviour.

cards.notes:
Authored 2026-08-26 under ruling R-020, which reopened CRIT-11 on the grounds that a guard proven on one execution path does not close a defect defined across all of them.

THE SUSPICION THAT PROMPTED THE REOPENING WAS WRONG AND THE REOPENING IS STILL RIGHT, and both halves matter. Forensics under R-012 established that CI DOES NOT POINT AT PRODUCTION AND CANNOT: the workflow starts its own Supabase stack, exports that stack URL and keys, references no repository secret, and gh secret list returns empty, so the repository has no secrets at all. Confirmed empirically from the log of run 33010883734, which shows NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL resolving to http://127.0.0.1:54321, not only by reading the YAML. Full report: docs/reports/forensics-20260826-product-count.md.

WHAT IS GENUINELY UNPROVEN is the refusal branch in CI. The guard EXECUTES on both paths, because globalSetup runs before every Playwright invocation, and that was CRIT-11 design intent. But CI always resolves to a local stack, so only the PASS path has ever run there. A green quality run proves the guard does not block a legitimate suite; it proves nothing about whether it would stop an illegitimate one.

THE FAILURE THIS LEAVES OPEN IS A FUTURE EDIT, not the present configuration. Someone adds a repository secret and wires NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL to it, for a preview environment or a smoke test, and the first thing that tells anyone the guard stopped enforcing is rows appearing on the client screen. The guard is correct today and nothing in CI would notice if it stopped being correct.

ALSO ESTABLISHED, AND WORTH KEEPING NEXT TO THIS CARD: zero rows have been written to the production project since CRIT-11 merged, in any table. Every row in every table predates 2026-08-26 02:50:44+00.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26 ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED AS WRITTEN: the refusal exercised in the SAME workflow that would otherwise stop enforcing, as a step and not a second job; the deliberate failure runs the GUARD DIRECTLY and never the Playwright suite; the production ref taken from the already-public committed blocklist so no secret was needed; static and runtime checks kept separate and both required; and no change to the guard itself.
WHY THE OBVIOUS TEST WOULD HAVE BEEN THE DANGEROUS ONE, and this is the whole design decision. The instinct is to point the Playwright suite at a production URL in CI and assert the run fails. That test is exactly as safe as the guard it tests: if the guard has already broken, which is the single scenario this card exists to detect, the suite starts and writes rows into the client project. It would report the defect BY CAUSING IT. Running the guard as its own process and asserting its exit code proves the identical thing, because the guard is the thing under test, and nothing else starts. Written into docs/LEARNINGS.md as a rule: to test a safety mechanism, exercise the mechanism, not the disaster it prevents.
THE STATIC HALF ASSERTS THE ONE LINE THAT MAKES THE GUARD EXIST AT ALL. globalSetup in playwright.config.ts is what causes the guard to run for every spec. Deleting that line disables it everywhere and breaks nothing visibly, so check 4 asserts it and was proved to fail on a copy with the line removed.
WHAT THIS CARD DID NOT FIND, AND SAYS SO: CI was never pointed at production. The forensics under R-020 established that the workflow starts its own Supabase stack, references no repository secret, and the repository has none. The defect closed here is narrower and real: nothing would have NOTICED if that changed.
